purpose: Owner correction: retain both natural winding road character and generous width for tower mazes; replace the rejected oval/plaza study
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create ONE NEW original level-design reference for the existing Not 3A Game. Use the two provided original project images only for the hand-painted cartoon visual style and the identities of the red portal, cyan soul objective, towers, skeletons and terrain materials. DO NOT copy their map geometry.
The owner wants a NATURAL WINDING WIDE ROAD. Prior versions failed in two opposite ways: a skinny angular zigzag, then an almost straight oval paved plaza. This new composition must clearly read as an organically meandering ROAD while staying generously wide enough for player-built tower mazes.
A single broad old gray stone/earth road winds from an intact dark slate portal with red vortex near the upper-right to the blue soul sphere under an ice dome near the lower-left. Draw an OPEN ASYMMETRICAL S with two CLEAR LARGE ALTERNATING CURVES. The road's central axis must visibly turn left, then right, then approach the goal, like an old road following meadow contours. Make the curves continuously rounded with unequal natural radii, not hard Z corners. Both road edges must follow those curves. There must be substantial rolling green land between the receding arms, and each bend must remain distinct; do not let the band merge into one central plaza. The whole road and both endpoints fit in the frame.
WIDTH IS ESSENTIAL: the road is a broad battle/building tract, typically around ten to fourteen ONE-TOWER FOOTPRINTS across, with no narrow chokepoint. At outer bends it opens a little into irregular shoulder pockets; between bends it eases inward only modestly. Several transverse partial tower rows and a continuous enemy passage could fit within its width. The player will form small zigzags with towers inside this large winding road later. Do not draw a single-file walking trail. Preserve abundant gray buildable paving around every shown tower. Landmark footing is about three tower cells wide, so the road width must visibly be several landmark-base widths, not only one.
NATURAL SHAPE AND EDGES: irregular worn, slightly crumbled gray paving stones, gray compacted earth showing through missing slabs, weeds and soft turf invading uneven shoulders. Staggered organic green tongues on some inside bends. No regular curbs, perfect parallel ruler edges, rectangular fields, smooth oval/capsule-shaped plazas, billiard-table outlines or geometric lawn islands. Stone courses may subtly follow the road's curves; keep the wide walking/building surface unobstructed. No elevated terrain collision, bridges, cliffs, new props or structural walls across the road.
Match the project's soft readable outlined cartoon fantasy art: warm yellow-green short turf with earth pockets, sparse daisies/shrubs and roadside ruin fragments, familiar conifers, pale boulders and dark rusty ore on surrounding green ground. The world continues beyond the image borders. Fixed steep elevated orthographic camera, no horizon, consistent daylight; pull back enough to see the entire long meandering battlefield. The endpoints should feel about twice as far apart at shared object scale as in the original close test scene; this is an illustrative layout, not a pixel-measured plan.
For scale put THREE familiar small defenses on the road: two red-roof timber Rapid watchtowers and one stone-enclosed wooden spoon catapult, separated near different bends. Leave almost all the road unbuilt. A handful of small ragged cartoon skeletons follow the winding center region from portal toward objective, without a painted trail. No rows of twenty towers, maze overlay, arrows, grid overlay, HUD, labels or layout-diagram graphics.
One understated title only: "E — NATURAL WIDE ROAD". Original project artwork, no third-party game scenery or branding.
